name: Dhankar
tagline: Spiti's old capital, a gompa on a cliff above two rivers
meta_description: Dhankar guide: the cliff-top gompa at 3,894 m, Dhankar Lake hike, Lhalung village, homestays, taxi costs from Kaza and Tabo, and altitude tips.
summary: Dhankar is a village at 3,894 m whose old gompa clings to a ridge 300 m above the meeting of the Spiti and Pin rivers. It was Spiti's capital in the 17th century. Visit on the drive between Tabo and Kaza, hike to Dhankar Lake, and stay a night in a homestay if you want the place to yourself.
intro: Dhankar means fort on a cliff, and the name is exact. The old gompa and the ruins of the fort stand on a crumbling spur of eroded earth pillars, about 300 m above the confluence of the Spiti and Pin rivers. From here the rulers of Spiti could see anyone coming up either valley, which is why Dhankar served as the capital in the 17th century.

The old monastery is fragile. In 2006 the World Monuments Fund listed it among the 100 most endangered sites in the world, and conservation work has continued since. Most of the monks now live in the newer monastery below the village, where the Dalai Lama inaugurated a teaching temple in 2009. The old gompa remains open to visitors, with dark rooms, old paintings and a view that makes the climb worth it.

The village itself is small, with stone and mud houses, fields of barley and peas, and a handful of homestays. A steep trail climbs about an hour to Dhankar Lake, a small high pool with views of the Manirang range. Dhankar sits 8 km up a side road from Schilling on NH-505, which makes it an easy stop between Tabo and Kaza.
facts: Cliff-top gompa, old fort, Dhankar Lake, confluence view

highlights.title: The old cliff-top gompa
highlights.text: The old gompa is built into a ridge of eroded earth pillars, with small dark rooms, faded paintings and narrow ladders. Walk softly, do not lean on walls, and leave a donation: conservation here depends on visitors and the monastery.

highlights.title: The view over two rivers
highlights.text: From the gompa roof you look down on the confluence of the Spiti and Pin rivers, braided across a wide gravel bed. Late afternoon light makes the earth pillars glow.

highlights.title: Dhankar Lake hike
highlights.text: A steep trail climbs about an hour from the village to a small high lake, often still and reflecting the peaks of the Manirang range. Start in the morning and carry water.

highlights.title: The new monastery
highlights.text: Below the village, the newer monastery houses most of Dhankar's monks. The Dalai Lama inaugurated its teaching temple in July 2009. Prayers here are easier to attend than in the old gompa.

highlights.title: Homestay night under the fort
highlights.text: A few homestays in Dhankar let you see the gompa at dawn and dusk without the day cars. Simple rooms, dinner with the family, and a quiet village once the road empties.

field_notes.fact: In Tibetan, dhang or dang means cliff and kar or khar means fort, so Dhangkar means fort on a cliff. The gompa sits on a spur about 300 m above the confluence of the Spiti and Pin rivers.
Dhankar was the traditional capital of the Spiti valley kingdom in the 17th century, and parts of the gompa's architecture are thought to go back to the 12th century.
In 2006 the World Monuments Fund named Dhankar Gompa one of the 100 most endangered sites in the world, which prompted conservation work by the Dhangkar Initiative.

local_word.meaning: fort or palace, the second half of the name Dhankar

costs: Tea and snacks at the village cafe

how_to_reach.text: The nearest airport is Bhuntar near Kullu; then Manali to Kaza (one day) and 33 km on to Dhankar. Shimla airport serves the Kinnaur approach via Tabo.
Buses between Kaza and Tabo pass Schilling at the foot of the Dhankar road; from there it is 8 km uphill. Shared taxis are easier. Check current timings in Kaza.
Dhankar is about 33 km from Kaza and 32 km from Tabo, the last 8 km a steep, narrow climb from Schilling on NH-505. Allow 1–1.5 hours from Kaza.

where_to_stay: Saver: a few family homestays and simple guesthouses in Dhankar charge about ₹1,200–2,200 a person with dinner and breakfast; bathrooms are basic and hot water often comes by bucket. Comfort and signature: there is no hotel of that standard here, so we visit Dhankar on a day trip between Tabo and Kaza and stay in Kaza or Rangrik. If you sleep in Dhankar, remember it is higher than Kaza at 3,894 m; do it after acclimatising, not on your first night in Spiti.
tips: Combine Dhankar with Tabo on the same day; they are about 32 km apart.
Climb to the lake in the morning; afternoon winds are strong and cold.
The old gompa is fragile: do not lean on walls or climb on the roofs outside marked areas.
Photography rules vary room by room; ask before using your camera indoors.
Drive the 8 km Schilling road slowly; it is steep, narrow and prone to rockfall.

experiences.title: Inside the cliff-top gompa of Dhankar
experiences.summary: Climb through the narrow rooms of Spiti's old capital monastery, perched 300 m above two rivers, and see why conservationists have spent two decades trying to save it.
body: The old gompa is a stack of small rooms and passages built into a ridge of eroded earth. Ladders connect the levels, and some rooms hold old paintings and statues dimly lit through small windows. A caretaker monk usually opens it in the day and collects a small fee or donation.

Move carefully. The building is fragile, and in 2006 it was named among the 100 most endangered sites in the world. Do not lean on walls, sit on ledges or climb outside marked areas. Ask before photographing indoors; flash is never appropriate.

Finish on the terrace for the view over the Spiti–Pin confluence. Then walk down to the newer monastery below the village to see where the monks live and pray today. If you have time and energy, add the hike to Dhankar Lake.

faqs.q: Is Dhankar Monastery safe to visit?
faqs.a: Yes, in the areas open to visitors. Follow the caretaker's directions, use the ladders carefully and stay off roofs and ledges.

faqs.q: Is there an entry fee at Dhankar?
faqs.a: Usually a small fee or donation, about ₹50–100. It supports the monastery and its conservation.

faqs.q: Can seniors climb inside Dhankar Gompa?
faqs.a: The ladders are steep and the altitude is 3,894 m. Fit seniors manage with care; others may prefer the terrace and the new monastery.

experiences.title: Hike to Dhankar Lake
experiences.summary: A steep climb of about an hour from Dhankar village to a small high lake with views of the Manirang peaks. Short, hard at altitude, and rewarding on a still morning.
body: The trail starts above the village and climbs steadily on a dusty path, gaining roughly 250 m to the lake. It is not long, about 2–3 km each way, but at nearly 4,000 m every step counts. Most people take an hour up and 45 minutes down.

Go in the morning. The water is calm before the wind rises, and the reflections of the Manirang range are best. Carry water, a warm layer, sunscreen and a snack. There are no shops or shelters on the way.

Stay on the path, take your rubbish back, and do not swim or wash in the lake, which local people regard as sacred. If you feel dizzy or develop a strong headache, turn back; the lake will be there next time.

faqs.q: How difficult is the Dhankar Lake trek?
faqs.a: Short but steep, about an hour up at nearly 4,000 m. Fit walkers manage it easily after acclimatising in Kaza or Tabo.

faqs.q: Do I need a guide for Dhankar Lake?
faqs.a: No, the path is clear in summer. A guide is useful if snow covers the trail early or late in the season.

faqs.q: Can I camp at Dhankar Lake?
faqs.a: Ask locally. We recommend sleeping in the village instead to protect the lake and its fragile surroundings.

experiences.title: Lhalung village and its old temple
experiences.cost: Taxi from Dhankar ₹1,500–2,500 return; donation at the temple
experiences.summary: A quiet side valley above Dhankar leads to Lhalung, a farming village with an old temple full of clay figures. Few visitors, green fields and a slow pace.
body: From Dhankar, a road continues into the Lingti side valley towards Lhalung, a village of stone houses and terraced fields. It sees far fewer visitors than Key or Langza, and in summer the village is busy with the harvest of peas and barley.

Lhalung's old temple is known for its clay figures and painted interior. Opening depends on the caretaker, so ask in the village and be ready to wait. Leave a donation and follow photography rules inside.
Walk the lanes, drink tea in a homestay, and return to Dhankar or continue down to Kaza. Treat it as a half-day for travellers who want a village without crowds, and go in a group to split the taxi.

faqs.q: How do I get to Lhalung?
faqs.a: By taxi from Dhankar or Kaza on a side road into the Lingti valley. There is no regular bus; share the car to save money.
No. A caretaker opens it on request. Ask in the village and allow time.
A few families take guests in summer. Book through your Kaza or Dhankar host.

faqs.q: How do I reach Dhankar from Kaza?
faqs.a: Take a taxi from Kaza, about 33 km and 1–1.5 hours, costing ₹2,500–3,500 for a return trip. Buses between Kaza and Tabo pass Schilling at the bottom of the 8 km Dhankar road, but there is no regular bus up to the village, so shared taxis are easier.

faqs.q: Is it worth staying overnight in Dhankar?
faqs.a: Yes, if you like quiet. After the day cars leave, the village is still, and dawn on the gompa is beautiful. Homestays are simple, with basic bathrooms. Most travellers see it in two hours on the way between Tabo and Kaza, which also works well.

Dhankar is at 3,894 m, about 240 m higher than Kaza. Sleep here after acclimatising, not on your first night in Spiti. The lake above is close to 4,140 m. Drink water, walk slowly, and talk to your doctor about altitude before you travel.

It is built on a ridge of eroded earth pillars that crumble over time, and its walls are old mud and stone. In 2006 the World Monuments Fund listed it among the 100 most endangered sites in the world, and conservation work has been ongoing since.

faqs.q: How long is the Dhankar Lake trek?
faqs.a: About 2–3 km each way with a climb of roughly 250 m, taking an hour up and 45 minutes down. Start early, carry water and a warm layer, and turn back if you feel unwell.

faqs.q: Is there mobile network in Dhankar?
faqs.a: BSNL and Jio usually have weak signal in the village. Do not depend on it for payments or bookings; carry cash and confirm your plans in Kaza or Tabo.

faqs.q: Can I see Dhankar and Tabo in one day?
faqs.a: Yes. They are about 32 km apart. Spend the morning in Tabo and the afternoon in Dhankar, or the other way round, and reach Kaza by evening. It is one of the most rewarding days in Spiti.
Yes for a day visit. Children enjoy the view and the ladders, but hold small hands on the old gompa's steps and terraces. Skip the lake hike with young children unless they are well acclimatised.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit Dhankar?
faqs.a: May to October. June and September are the best balance of open roads and fewer visitors. In July and August, landslides on the approach roads can delay travel. Winter visits are possible from Shimla but cold and snowy.
